title: Use transaction markers without assuming replay suppression
brief: Application transaction markers are useful persisted coordination metadata. At this pin, repeating the same marker on sequential appends does not automatically suppress the second write.

choices.choose_when: An application coordinates checkpoints with committed table state
choices.tradeoff: Design race/retry handling; a pre-read alone is not atomic deduplication

choices.choose_when: Every invocation is intended to add records

choices.candidate: Domain-key merge or externally coordinated ingestion
choices.choose_when: You need a stronger uniqueness/replay policy
choices.tradeoff: Define key semantics and concurrent ownership explicitly

claims.statement: Two sequential writes with the same application marker version 7 produced two rows and table version 1; transaction_version returned Some(7).
A txn marker participates in transaction state and conflict logic, but the marker alone is not an exactly-once ingestion algorithm.
After an ambiguous error, reload and inspect the application marker, commit metadata/history and data outcome before choosing whether to retry. Retention may limit the evidence available.
A stale writer carrying the same application marker conflicted after the competing writer committed; this does not change the separately observed sequential replay behavior.

implementation: Persist a meaningful application batch identity in commit properties and define how it maps to source offsets.
Specify concurrent ownership, conflict handling and reconciliation, then test duplicate delivery and failures after publication.
effects: may append duplicate rows if retried
errors: A repeated marker and a retryable storage/transaction failure are different conditions.
unknowns: No distributed exactly-once protocol or external checkpoint service is qualified by the local tests.
